newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended near their lows on origin sales which drove benchmark March to a new contract low of $1,212 per tonne, down $15 from Friday's close. May lost $19 to close at $1,183 per tonne. News the coffee crop in Brazil's top-growing state of Minas Gerais was unaffected by recent heavy rains was within expectation and had little impact on the market. In New York arabica futures closed lower in a technical correction to the market's recent uptrend. March lost 2.20 cents/lb to close at 114.05 cents/lb, while May gave up 1.90 cents/lb to close at 112.45 cents/lb. US certified coffee stocks showed a surprising drop during the week ended January 3, which could underpin prices on Tuesday. Overall however, traders are still convinced that larger quantities of new crop supplies should become available this quarter helping to alleviate, at least temporarily, some of the tightness that had been experienced.

UNITED STATES - US certified coffee stocks fell by 1,607 60-kg bags to 32,458 bags (34,065 bags) during the week ended January 3, 1997. Stocks in New York and San Francisco remained unchanged at 778 and 0 bags respectively. Stocks in New Orleans fell by 857 bags to 6,911 bags (7,768 bags) while stocks in Miami showed a decline of 750 bags to 24,769 bags (25,519 bags).

UNITED STATES - Coffee roastings totalled about 465,000 60-kg bags during the week ended December 21, down from 475,000 bags the previous week and compared to 360,000 bags in the corresponding week one year ago, Complete Coffee Coverage said. Cumulative roastings totalled 17.5 million bags versus 16.78 million bags in the same year-ago period.

ICO - Coffee exports to all destinations by exporting members of the International Coffee Organization in November 1996 totalled 6.077 million 60-kg bags, slightly up on the 6.019 million bags shipped in November 1995. That brought total exports in the first two months of coffee year 1996/97 (October/November) up to 12.042 million bags, up from 11.236 million bags shipped during the same two months in 1995. Exports of Colombian milds in October/November 1996 increased by 5.4 per cent against the same period the previous year while shipments of other milds were down by 21.33 per cent. Shipments of Brazilian and other arabicas increased by 75.08 per cent while shipments of robustas were down by 13.20 per cent. Colombia's market share in October/November 1996 dropped to 18.77 per cent down from 19.07 per cent while Brazil, due to significantly higher shipments, was able to increase its market share to 32.73 per cent from 19.37 per cent in October/November 1995.

NORWAY - Norway imported 55,678 bags of coffee in November 1996, 14 per cent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 667,400 bags, 12 per cent more than was imported in the same year-ago period. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped sharply by 18 per cent to 662,100 bags. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/November 1996 were Brazil (158,900 vs 237,100 bags) and Colombia (146,000 vs 126,500 bags).
